scenes.text: [whispers] See this code? It shipped three sprints ago... and it has never run. [laughs] Spot why?
One typo, and every Flagsmith SDK quietly says: off. No error. Because your flags live in a dashboard, five clicks away from your code.
So I built FlagLens: self-hosted Flagsmith, live inside VS Code. It does three things. It knows what runs. It proves your rules. And it's live.
Make up, make seed: real open-source Flagsmith in Docker, demo included. Click connect... and every flag shows its state, in every environment.
One. It knows what runs. Code that can't run here? Greyed out, like an inactive ifdef. Switch to Production, and it updates. Only when it's certain.
Pick a user, say Alice, our beta tester. Now every line shows what she gets, and why. Flagsmith's own rules, run locally: fifteen thousand checks against the real server. Zero misses.
Two. It proves your rules. This EU override can never fire. Pro plan catches those users first.
So fix it, right here. Move it up, confirm... [excited] and the warning's gone. Written straight to Flagsmith.
Three. It's live. Someone flips a flag in the Flagsmith dashboard... and seconds later, your editor knows. The whole handler just went grey.
And when monitoring marks a flag unhealthy, Flagsmith Feature Health tells FlagLens. It's right there on the code, and in the confirmation, before anyone touches it.
Every change is safe. One click in Development, and the shop updates. Production? [laughs] Nope. You type the flag name first.
Testing six flags? Ninety-six combinations... or seven runs that cover every pair. Provably the minimum.
Plus code references in Flagsmith, overrides for one user, versioned environments, drift, typos, stale flags. All on open-source Flagsmith.
FlagLens. It knows what runs, it proves your rules, and it's live. Make up, make seed, and you're in. [laughs softly] Go try it.
